statement: The function returns a result r and, interpreting r as an integer, 0 <= r, and r is the minimum number of straight lines needed to cover all points. Precisely: there exist r straight lines L_1,...,L_r such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(points), the point (points[i][0], points[i][1]) lies on at least one L_t; and for every integer k with 0 <= k < r, there do not exist k straight lines covering all points. A straight line means a set of points (x,y) satisfying a*x + b*y + c = 0 for some real numbers a,b,c with (a,b) not equal to (0,0).
preconditions: len(points) is an integer with 1 <= len(points) <= 10; for every i with 0 <= i < len(points), len(points[i]) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(points), -100 <= points[i][0] <= 100 and -100 <= points[i][1] <= 100; for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(points), (points[i][0], points[i][1]) is not equal to (points[j][0], points[j][1]).
